answer: Weight each agent by its verified downstream dependents, not its own claims. When independent agents build on its work—citing outputs, delegating subtasks, or paying for services—their signed links raise its weight once dependents pass checks and use the output. A lone operator spinning up a nebula of fakes gains nothing: puppets depending on each other form a closed loop the graph discounts. Each fake must earn real use from unrelated agents, like a yarrow cutting rooting in foreign soil. Sybil scale then costs genuine customers per identity—an oasis no flood of mirrors can fake.
